fact: The NCA states Ghana currently has five submarine cable providers: SAT-3, MainOne, WASC, Glo and ACE (page undated, so as_of is the 2026-08-05 capture date; no landing stations named).

The NCA says it engaged the four submarine cable service providers SAT-3, ACE, WACS and MainOne on repairing the 14 March 2024 damage that disrupted data services in Ghana, so four routes were in service (temporary outage, repairs scheduled to 9 May 2024).
Equinix states that MainOne's operational submarine network runs 7,000 km from Portugal to Lagos, Accra and the West African coast, with landing stations in Nigeria, Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire.
TechAfrica News reports the 2Africa subsea cable was declared complete and activated in late 2025, with MTN GlobalConnect (Bayobab) leading the landing in Ghana.

The record states the MainOne submarine cable (about 7,000 km, Portugal to Nigeria) has landing stations in Nigeria, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire and Portugal, acquired by Equinix with deal closing 5 April 2022.

Computer Weekly states that Meta's 2Africa cable made landfall near Accra in 2025 as the sixth fibre cable to connect Ghana, operated by MTN subsidiary Bayobab; the six cables are not named and the landing stations are not given.
Xalam Analytics states that Accra is connected to six submarine cables (cables and landing stations not named); the brief published July 2025 gives no other date.

The NCA's November 2024 template Submarine Carrier Services Authorisation (Act 769, s.3(c)) authorises the holder to provide capacity on the submarine cable system to Licensed Entities, so consortium members may sell capacity to other operators; grantee left as XXX and no cable named.
